nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.rationale: Kalshi's KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS rules give only the team name and event date (rules_secondary is empty), so the format comes from league material. Verified for 2026 (NBA release wording as returned by search; consistent across outlets): four teams of three (two current NBA players plus one legend), seven designated spots in a fixed order, one team on the floor at a time with 70 seconds, two rounds (all four in round 1, the top two repeat in a final), and the champion is the team with the higher final-round score. The per-spot point values, the tie rules and the per-spot attempt mechanics are NOT verified from a primary document read by this project (the league rules PDF host is unreachable from the research session), so they are carried below as explicit UNVERIFIED parameters and the input must not simulate scores until they are filled from the PDF. Legends have no current shooting data, so team skill mixes current catch-and-shoot rates with old evidence; tempo matters as in the 3PT contest.
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.measurement: VERIFIED FORMAT FIELDS (2026, league release wording relayed by web search; see evidence_zblk/NBA_u10_shooting_stars.json): 4 teams x 3 players (2 current players + 1 legend); 7 designated spots shot in a fixed order; teams shoot one at a time; clock = 70 s per team per round; round 1 = all four teams, top two advance; final = the same timed challenge; champion = higher final-round score (round-1 score only decides advancement). UNVERIFIED PARAMETERS (must be read from the league's 2026 Kia Shooting Stars rules PDF before any simulation; the input never assumes them): (U1) points per spot: reported but unconfirmed values by spot 1-7 = 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4 (right-lane layup/dunk, 18-ft right baseline, right elbow, right-wing three, top of key, left-corner three, long-range three); only spots 1-3 and 7 were returned as quoted fragments of the PDF; (U2) advancement tie rule: reported 30-second shoot-off by secondary outlets, not confirmed; (U3) final-round tie rule: sources conflict (replay of the whole final round versus another 1:10 on the clock); (U4) attempts per spot per player, whether the circuit repeats after spot 7 inside 70 s, passer mechanics and what counts when the clock expires mid-shot; (U5) whether the same rules apply in other editions. Estimation once U1-U4 are filled: current players: P(make) by spot from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile; legend component: last five career seasons' 3P% and FT% with an age discount of 1.5 points of 3P% per year since retirement, shrunk to past legends' contest make rate with k = 50 shots, plus a shot-tempo term for the legend's attempts inside the clock; simulate 20,000 contests including the round-1 selection of two of four and report P(win) with the tie rules as labelled branches. Until then output only a labelled rank composite. CONTRACT CONSTRAINT: KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS settles on which named team wins the contest, so U1 and U4 matter because they set both teams' score distributions (a 4-point spot is worth twice a 2-point spot); U2 matters only when two teams tie for the second final slot; U3 matters only if the final ends level; Kalshi's text has no tie, shoot-off or team-change clause, so a tie is settled by whatever the league declares.
